arxiv.titleZh: 一个框架诊断所有：面向孟加拉语 LLM 幻觉的分层基准
arxiv.summaryZh: 针对低资源语言幻觉研究数据集碎片化、标注不可比的问题，构建孟加拉语幻觉检测基准 Alikbachan，沿文化距离、六类任务与五族 32 种幻觉分类法三轴交叉分层，含 2516 条采集测试集与 5000 条配额构建的金标集。四个零样本 LLM 判官跨层 macro-F1 差异超 30 点，概率排序尚可（ROC-AUC 0.74–0.95）但明显过自信（ECE 0.04–0.29），语篇级遗漏是主要失败模式。竞赛吸引 222 支队伍、3566 次提交；同时参与两阶段的 25 支队伍中 24 支在第二阶段掉分（均值 −17.6），而零样本判官均有提升，第一阶段排名对第二阶段预测力很弱（Spearman ρ=0.35）。

arxiv.title: What If Chain-of-Thought Is Not Enough?
arxiv.abstract: Reasoning capabilities in large language models have evolved from prompting-based methods to internalized model behaviors. In this paper, we investigate whether the internal thinking model of an LLM can be deliberately changed and whether such a change is beneficial. Instead of relying on Chain-of-Thought, we train models to follow Question--Option--Criteria (QOC), a structured decision process that decomposes a task into explicit questions, competing options, and evaluation criteria. We present a three-generation development pipeline that ranges from a basic QOC decision core to richer answer synthesis and statistically enriched QOC reasoning. We then evaluate the resulting models with respect to both internal consistency and output quality. Across the reported experiments, QOC-based fine-tuning improves answer quality relative to non-fine-tuned base models and yields particularly strong gains once models are large enough to execute the underlying QOC computations reliably. The results suggest that the internal thinking model of an LLM is trainable and that structured alternatives to Chain-of-Thought can provide a promising path toward more reliable, interpretable, and task-adapted decision support.
arxiv.titleZh: 如果思维链还不够呢?
arxiv.summaryZh: 针对思维链(CoT)提示难以内化为稳定模型行为的问题，该工作提出 Question–Option–Criteria(QOC)结构化决策过程，把任务拆成显式问题、候选选项与评估标准，并用三阶段生成式流水线训练模型:从基础 QOC 决策核心，到更丰富的答案综合，再到统计增强的 QOC 推理。评估兼顾内部一致性与输出质量，结果显示 QOC 微调相对未微调基座模型提升答案质量，且当模型规模足以可靠执行 QOC 计算时增益尤为明显。这说明 LLM 的内部思维模式可被训练改变，结构化替代 CoT 有望带来更可靠、可解释、贴合任务需求的决策支持。
arxiv.reason: 结构化推理替代 CoT 的后训练工作，方法清晰但实验细节有限

embodied.title: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience
embodied.abstract: A central goal of humanoid robotics is for robots to perform the everyday work people do in homes and workplaces. Existing egocentric video datasets cover many of these activities but provide little synchronized whole-body motion data for learning loco-manipulation at scale. We build Awaken-Human, which pairs approximately 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body human motion and covers more than 100 skills. Building on this, we also introduce Awaken-HI (Humanoid Intelligence), a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert. We show that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert. Increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks. After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, Awaken-HI achieves a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight individual tasks and outperforms GR00T N1.7 and $π_{0.5}$ in both individual and long-horizon evaluations. The same policy generalizes to objects unseen during robot post-training and to new pairings of familiar objects and destinations.
embodied.titleZh: Awaken-HI：以全身人类经验扩展人形智能
embodied.summaryZh: 现有第一视角视频数据集缺少同步的全身运动数据，难以支撑大规模loco-manipulation学习。工作构建Awaken-Human数据集，将约5万小时第一视角立体视频与同步全身人体运动配对，覆盖100余项技能；并在此基础上提出VLA模型Awaken-HI，通过共享action expert同时预测原始人体运动与重定向后的机器人动作，使人类轨迹直接监督该模块。实验显示人类预训练数据增加会按经验scaling law降低留出集机器人动作预测误差，并提升真机下游任务成功率；全量预训练并在T800适配后，八个单项任务平均成功率达93.75%，在单项与长程评测中均优于GR00T N1.7与π0.5，且可泛化到未见物体及未见过的物体与目的地组合。
embodied.reason: 人形VLA旗舰技术报告，5万小时全身数据与scaling law，直击VLA训练方向

embodied.title: Alignment Drives Reuse: Learning Generalizable Robot-Use Agents from Heterogeneous Experience
embodied.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate broad generalization across tasks and domains. However, comparable generalization in robot manipulation remains challenging. Heterogeneity in robot embodiments, task formulations, geometric conventions, and action interfaces fragments interaction experience across benchmarks and hardware. We rethink robot skill learning through alignment: Can heterogeneous interactions across benchmarks and embodiments jointly improve one shared skillset for robot manipulation? We propose UniCraft, a framework for learning robot manipulation skills by aligning heterogeneous settings. Specifically, UniCraft represents observed scene geometry using consistent coordinate conventions and aligns sensing and control interfaces across robots. It organizes tasks from different benchmarks in a canonical format, allowing interaction feedback to jointly refine shared skills and the orchestration policy that guides their selection and composition, without any demonstrations or model weight updates. We interleave tasks from 3 benchmarks and 6 embodiments, collecting 2,700 learning rollouts per agent model. During training, UniCraft improves pooled task success on unseen scenarios and tasks by 9-28 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO, 10.8-13.3 on RoboTwin 2.0, and 3.1-14.4 on RoboCasa365 (Epochs 1-3). After training, with the learned skills frozen, UniCraft demonstrates zero-shot transfer across 4 new robot embodiments and 5 additional agent models on robosuite and RoboDojo.
embodied.titleZh: 对齐驱动复用：从异构经验中学习可泛化的机器人使用智能体
embodied.summaryZh: 跨benchmark与跨本体的交互经验因本体、任务表述、几何约定与动作接口不一致而割裂，机器人操作难以获得VLM级泛化。UniCraft用统一坐标约定表示场景几何，对齐各机器人的感知与控制接口，并把不同benchmark的任务组织为规范格式，使交互反馈在无示教、不更新权重的情况下同时改进共享技能库与负责技能选择、组合的编排策略。在3个benchmark、6种本体上各采集2700条rollout，训练1–3轮即在未见场景上提升9–28（LIBERO-PRO）、10.8–13.3（RoboTwin 2.0）、3.1–14.4（RoboCasa365）个百分点；冻结技能后可零样本迁移到4种新本体与5个新智能体模型。
embodied.reason: 机器人智能体框架＋跨本体对齐复用，直接命中具身智能体方向

embodied.title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach
embodied.abstract: Generalist robot policies execute atomic skills reliably but fail when the same skills are composed into long-horizon tasks. Self-improvement from the policy's own experience does not close this gap: experience collected by the policy alone stays within its own distribution and reproduces what it can already do. We show that what the policy lacks is not a skill but the next step. We present CoachSI, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action. Successful coached rollouts are relabeled in hindsight with the original task instruction and used to fine-tune the policy. The fine-tuned policy is then deployed on its own. On states where a World Action Model and a Vision-Language-Action model have stalled, naming the next step raises subgoal completion by 4.6x over the unchanged task instruction, and the frozen VLM supplies it from the same camera images the policy sees. After fine-tuning, unassisted success on long-horizon tasks in unseen scenes rises from 47.4% to 59.3%, 9.8 points above fine-tuning on human demonstrations and 7.3 points above fine-tuning on self-collected successes at an equal data budget. With a coach that sees only camera images, it reaches 56.8%, above both baselines. The gain is obtained with the action backbone frozen: language coaching teaches the policy what should happen next, and the skills it already has do the rest.
embodied.titleZh: CoachSI：以语言教练实现机器人策略的自我改进

embodied.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
embodied.abstract: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.
embodied.titleZh: AgentRoboCritic：理解前沿智能体在直接机器人控制上的能力
embodied.summaryZh: 前沿多模态智能体已能绕过高层原语、直接用底层数值动作控制机器人，但现有基准只报告 episode 级成功率，看不出成功从何而来、失败发生在哪里。AgentRoboCritic 让策略智能体在每个动作旁声明局部意图，由 critic 对照意图评估动作结果与失败模式，并在 12 个操作基准上做动作级分析：前沿智能体具备局部失败后的闭环恢复、跨场景语义 grounding 与零样本操作能力，但抓取、对齐等物理执行仍是瓶颈。工作释放 12,844 条标注动作数据集与微调 critic Muse-Glimmer-30B，失败模式准确率由 32.58% 升至 74.24%。

embodied.title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
embodied.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution. As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data. We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations. All data are generated by a scalable, fully automatic pipeline that combines grasp generation, motion planning, and closed-loop throw optimization under randomized physical properties. We evaluate three representative VLAs, GR00T N1.7, DynamicVLA, and ForceVLA, and find that all achieve success rates below 3\%. Our analysis reveals two key bottlenecks: limited robustness of pretrained models, which causes most failures before the throw, and physical blindness, as providing ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success. Experiments on a humanoid robot and in the real world show the same failure patterns. We hope PhyDEX will drive the development of physically grounded robot policies.
embodied.titleZh: PhyDEX:基于动态外部灵巧操作的视觉-语言-动作模型物理推理基准
embodied.summaryZh: 现有VLA基准大多只考察夹爪与物体的接触，忽略重力、摩擦、惯性、质量分布等环境交互，难以判断策略是真懂物理还是在插值训练数据。PhyDEX以抛掷任务切入动态外部灵巧性:机器人需推断物体质量、质心与摩擦，把物体送到运动学工作空间之外。数据由抓取生成、运动规划与闭环抛掷优化组成的全自动流水线产出，含35K轨迹(143小时)、九个任务、100个场景，覆盖均匀、不规则与动态质量物体及静止、多目标、移动目的地。评测GR00T N1.7、DynamicVLA与ForceVLA，成功率均低于3%;给出真值物理参数后成功率约翻倍，暴露预训练鲁棒性不足与物理盲两个瓶颈。

embodied.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
embodied.abstract: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.
embodied.titleZh: Mind2Act World：面向机器人操作中具身心智、物理动作与心智-动作组合的诊断基准

embodied.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
embodied.abstract: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves effective navigation with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain. Rather than teaching the brain to predict geometric goals, we equip it with a semantic tool-calling interface for conveying movement decisions to an action expert in natural language. We first adapt the action expert to carry out these movement requests, then jointly improve the brain's movement decisions and the action expert's continuous execution through closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL). Trained on the same navigation episodes, ZeroVLN substantially outperforms representative SFT-based hierarchical VLN methods on standard VLN-CE (continuous environments) benchmarks, while inducing only minor changes to the brain's weights and largely preserving its general capabilities. To our knowledge, ZeroVLN is the first slow-fast VLN framework with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain, and the first to jointly optimize its slow and fast policies through closed-loop agentic RL in VLN-CE.
embodied.titleZh: ZeroVLN：无需对VLM大脑做监督微调即可学习导航
embodied.summaryZh: 代表性视觉语言导航（VLN）方法将VLM大脑与可学习动作头耦合，并在导航域数据上微调VLM以预测几何目标，但这样会显著改动基座权重、削弱通用视觉能力。ZeroVLN采用慢-快导航框架，让VLM大脑通过语义工具调用接口，用自然语言把移动决策传给动作专家，先训练动作专家执行这些请求，再用闭环强化学习联合优化大脑的决策与专家的连续执行。在相同导航数据上训练后，该方法在VLN-CE基准上大幅超过代表性的SFT式分层VLN方法，同时只对大脑权重造成微小改动，基本保留其通用能力。这是首个VLM大脑零导航域SFT的慢-快VLN框架，也是首个在VLN-CE中用闭环智能体式RL联合优化快慢策略的工作，为保留基座模型通用能力的具身智能体后训练提供了可复用范式。

embodied.title: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
embodied.abstract: Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both. To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor. These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment. On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate. Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.
embodied.titleZh: 按需推理：面向长程机器人操作的高效智能体控制
embodied.summaryZh: 长程机器人操作中频繁调用多模态大模型带来显著延迟与 token 开销，难点在于判断何时需要智能体介入、错误应修正底层执行还是上层子任务规划。RoC 用在线任务状态监控器融合时序视觉观测与有序交互记忆，联合估计当前子任务进度并预测后继子任务，据此事件触发式唤醒高层推理，协同完成执行修复与计划修订，验证后的结果再驱动记忆更新与子任务切换，使常规执行留在低层策略、推理只用于需额外判断的决策。在 RMBench 上成功率较最强智能体基线提升 24.0 个百分点、token 消耗降低 65.3%，并比最强纯策略基线高 15.1 个百分点，三个真机长程任务亦验证其有效性。

embodied.title: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL
embodied.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can act as closed-loop robot-use agents (RUAs) by writing and executing control code through tool interfaces. However, turning an open-weight VLM into a high-performing embodied agent requires a complete post-training stack: out-of-the-box open VLMs fail completely at interactive tool contracts, strong frontier teachers are accessible only as black-box endpoints without exposed weights or token probabilities, and supervised imitation alone plateaus under rollout distribution shift. We present EmbodyAgent, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines: (1) a black-box data synthesis pipeline that queries a strong teacher under a forced think-then-code contract and filters trajectories by task success; (2) an SFT pipeline that distills the explanation-and-program targets into an open-weight 9B VLM with both vision and language encoders trainable; and (3) an online RL pipeline that optimizes student-generated episodes via group-relative advantage with a runtime-error-penalized outcome reward. All three pipelines share one primitive-free Python execution tool exposing only raw visual observation and seven-dimensional end-effector control, with no action decoder and no interface shift across stages. Under a strictly separated evaluation protocol on ten LIBERO Spatial tasks (disjoint state splits, greedy test-time decoding, training-only safeguards), held-out success on 100 test states rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 (after SFT) and 84/100 (after RL), while training rollout success climbs from 8.4% to 87.7% and median model calls per episode drop from 36 to 11. We further identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.

embodied.summaryZh: 开放权重 VLM 靠写代码调用工具即可充当闭环机器人智能体，但基座模型在工具契约上直接失败，前沿教师只能黑盒调用，纯模仿在 rollout 分布漂移下饱和。EmbodyAgent 用三条流水线补齐：按「先思考再写代码」契约查询黑盒教师并按成功过滤轨迹，把解释与程序蒸馏进 9B VLM，再用组相对优势加运行时错误惩罚的结果奖励做在线 RL，三阶段共享同一 Python 执行工具（仅原始视觉观测与七维末端控制）。LIBERO Spatial 十个任务 100 个测试状态上成功率 0/100→14/100（SFT）→84/100（RL），单回合调用中位数 36→11，并识别出可执行代码上结果型 RL 的自强化运行时错误模式。

embodied.title: One View, One Action: Spatially Generalizable VLAs through Observation-Aligned Experts and Cross Graph Consistency
embodied.abstract: Multi-view vision-language-action (VLA) models still face challenges in spatial generalization, particularly under changes in camera viewpoints and robot initial states. These models typically receive action supervision only in the robot base frame, requiring them to implicitly learn the spatial correspondence between observations from each view and base-frame actions. We propose One View, One Action (OVOA-VLA), which learns to predict actions in each view's camera frame, allowing the same physical motion to provide diverse, observation-aligned supervision across views. OVOA-VLA jointly trains a base-frame expert and view-specific action experts, whose robot-state inputs and action targets are expressed in their respective camera frames. Two complementary directed attention graphs model both directions of interaction between the base and view-specific experts, jointly leveraging view-specific action supervision to improve base-frame prediction. Cross Graph Consistency further encourages agreement between the two graphs' base-frame predictions for the same sample. With the same multi-view inputs, the model supports both full and base-only inference. Experiments across multiple simulation benchmarks demonstrate improved manipulation performance and robustness to camera-viewpoint and robot-initialization perturbations. Full and base-only inference achieve average success rates of 88.1% and 85.7% on LIBERO-Plus, respectively. In real-world evaluations, base-only inference raises the average success rates from $π_{0.5}$'s 28.3% to 58.3% across three tasks under spatial distribution shifts.
embodied.titleZh: 一视图，一动作：通过观测对齐专家与跨图一致性实现空间可泛化的 VLA
embodied.summaryZh: 多视图 VLA 只在机器人基座坐标系下接受动作监督，模型必须隐式学习各视图观测与基座系动作之间的空间对应，导致相机视角与初始位姿变化时泛化困难。OVOA-VLA 改为在每个视图的相机坐标系下预测动作，使同一物理运动在各视图上提供观测对齐的多样监督；模型联合训练一个基座系专家与多个视图专属专家，并用两个互补的有向注意力图建模二者的双向交互，再由跨图一致性约束两图对同一样本的基座系预测趋于一致，支持完整多视图与仅基座两种推理。LIBERO-Plus 上两种推理平均成功率分别为 88.1% 与 85.7%，真机空间分布偏移下仅基座推理把 π0.5 的平均成功率从 28.3% 提升到 58.3%。
